result: INCOMPLETE: no-swap kernel gap settled (+5k was the bench's own 4 KiB .bss buffer, fixed: now -6k vs merge-base, user +8); plant WARN fixed and CAUGHT; N100 timing: the AVX2-class swap costs +22-26 us per start (+14% exec_true_static) with memset rows unchanged: RULING NEEDED

gate.affected: kanon classed-slot-infra-5-gate (direct tier, final tree): running at write time

rulings.item: AVX2-class swap meets #3139's count (4 calls, +2 VMAs) but costs +22-26 us per process start on the N100 (+14% static true exec) and +56k kernel instructions on Broadwell, with no memset gain at 16-128 B
rulings.recommendation: do not enable the swap by default until the guard/mremap split is measured and cut, or an AVX2-page body repays it in real workloads

informational: xtask affected names a failed conformance program but never prints its stderr, so a plant msg on a conformance program's message cannot match without the cmd printing the file (done in this plants file)
a `bench --no-build --staged` run rewrites target/liella/bench/bench_times.tsv, a staged product, so the next --staged run in the same tree refuses it; unpack the tarball again per run
perf trace -s prints nothing for the claude user on kanon (no tracefs access), so the per-syscall time split needs an in-process probe
perf stat's user count reads +59 on the SSE2 class where the exact single-step tracer reads +8
improvement: the startup rows measure the bench program itself, so any static in cbench_startup.c moves start-up costs; a row-level check that the bench's .bss stays within the start-up's first touched page would have caught -4's buffer
next_step: ruling on the swap's per-start time cost; then a per-call time probe (openat/pread/close/mremap) on N100 and Broadwell and cut the largest part, or make the swap opt-in
